notes.title: NORCO 1.5.0
notes.content:
[i]Hello everyone! [/i]

We just released the 1.5.0 patch. The goal of this patch is to provide players with a smoother experience in general, particularly for those playing with a controller or on Steam Deck. We also made some light modifications to the game's third act that align more closely with our original vision, including a new animation panel leading into the credit roll. Here's a more detailed breakdown:

[u][b]General improvements:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Settings and menu buttons across the game now provide more visual feedback to better distinguish when a button is in focus.
[*] We addressed a bug that was preventing "expert mode" from persisting between saves. For those unfamiliar, this setting removes many signposts throughout the game. We also hid some additional signposts while in expert mode that are meant for casual players. 
[*] Several pieces of background artwork have been cleaned up and further detailed. 
[*] Some pieces of dialogue have been edited or removed for clarity, brevity and style, with an eye towards a more seamless, focused, and consistent reading experience.
[*] Players can now cancel out of nearly all "look" dialogues by right clicking or pressing the East controller button. This reduces the need to "click through" non-essential dialogue if the player isn’t interested or has already visited the dialogue node.
[*] The drone icons in the Shield puzzle map, previously red squares, have been replaced with animated sprites. 
[*] At several points, UI sound effects would drop due to a bug in our audio controller, particularly noticeable in the rocket environment. This is fixed.  
[*] Many bugs and edge cases across the game have been addressed. We hope that we've fixed nearly all softlocks.

[/list]
[u][b]Controller improvements:[/b][/u] 
[list]
[*] Players should notice a dramatic improvement in behavior when selecting elements within a scene using the directional pad. 
[*] Any players using a controller on a widescreen display will have likely experienced a bug in which the virtual mouse cursor was offset by some number of pixels. This is now fixed. 
[*] The boat controls in the puppetshow and lake sequences are tighter. The collision screenshake has been reduced. The boat drifts less and is generally easier to control.
[*] If using a controller, players are now prompted to view the "input diagram" before first entering gameplay following the game’s intro. This diagram gives an overview of various helper buttons, such as the ability to quickly select and cycle through pieces of the GUI.
[*] We discovered many edge cases in which the controller mode was not properly registered after certain sequences, and the player would momentarily lose the ability to use the directional pad and helper buttons. These edge cases have been addressed. 
[*] There are many other small improvements that should make playing the game with a controller more satisfying.
[/list]

[u][b]Third act modifications (light spoilers ahead):[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] We've made a few adjustments to the final act of the game, doing our best to keep these changes subtle and non-invasive. One addition is a brief animation panel preceding the credits, something we originally hoped to include before release but ran out of time. We’ve also edited and extended the final dialogue that leads into this animation.
[*] There's a dialogue choice provided to the player earlier in the third act that we felt the game should acknowledge. It now conditionally impacts a separate piece of dialogue that can be accessed in the "Delirious Dream" sequence prior to the game’s ending.
[/list]

[i]As always, thank you to everyone who has reported bugs and shared feedback. [/i]

With gratitude,
Geography of Robots

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/5bd1a6c25d1bb86d51f25586b56ed2a22e4dceb6.png[/img]

notes.title: NORCO 1.4.5 Update - Steam Deck Verification & More
notes.content:
Hello! We spent the past few weeks making NORCO Steam Deck verified. It's been compatible for a while, but in order to receive full verification, we made some slight UI modifications to support a 16x10 screen resolution. For now, this resolution is only supported on Steam Deck, but we'll make it available across all platforms in the future.

As always, we deeply appreciate the feedback and bug reports that we receive. Because of this community's help, the game has been able to grow and mature since its release. With a team as small as ours, the kind of support you've all shown is invaluable.

The best way to report issues and ensure that they get addressed in future patches is to use the bug reporting form available through Raw Fury's online portal: https://rawfury.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/1
Below are some additional updates and improvements included in the 1.4.5 patch, many of them in response to your reports. 

[b]1.4.5 Changelog[/b]
[list]
[*] Fix "screen flip" bug that occurs if a player simultaneously presses the dive and zoom buttons in the lake.
[*] Fix bug that causes the phone to disappear during choice selections when using the head drive app.
[*] Fix bug preventing controller input after engaging with the pigman hotspot in the lake.
[*] Make input diagram fade from the screen when any button is pressed.
[*] Fix attribution of "Templars in Acadiana" by Wilbur Stiles, which was mistakenly listed as "Templars in Louisiana" in the credits.
[*] Edit script for brevity and clarity, and to address typos in Acts II & III.
[*] Adjust the boat collision sensitivity during the puppet show and lake sequences.
[*] Support 16x10 screen resolution for Steam Deck.
[*] Reset/readjust UI on screen ratio change (this triggers when docking a Steam Deck).
[/list]

With abundant gratitude,
Yuts

notes.title: A year-end review, with gratitude
notes.content:
HELLO! We wanted to do a quick year-end review. A lot’s happened since the game came out in March. Reviews, bugs, interviews, podcasts, patches, vinyl pressing, prints... We're going to forget some stuff, but here's an attempt at a recap.

[h2]RELEASE & RECEPTION[/h2]
We released the game on March 24th. It feels like multiple years ago at this point. Anxiety was high. Being a neurotic group, we chalked the Tribeca win up to a strange fluke, and were confident that NORCO would get shredded by critics and reviewers. We went in prepared for this inevitability, armed only with our personal love and respect for what we created. We were floored by the positive reception from players as well as from [url=https://kotaku.com/game-pass-norco-review-adventure-southern-gothic-raw-fu-1848726472][b]Kotaku[/b][/url], [url=https://www.pcgamer.com/norco-review/#:~:text=There%20are%20few%20games%20in,experiences%20in%20the%20medium%20today.&text=A%20must%2Dplay%20for%20anyone%20interested%20in%20narrative%2Ddriven%20games.,-Alexis%20Ong][b]PC Gamer[/b][/url], [url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/n7nmxz/norco-review-greatness-in-the-tenacious-weirdos-who-live-there][b]Vice[/b][/url], [url=https://www.polygon.com/reviews/23025400/norco-review-point-and-click-adventure-windows-pc-mac-ending][b]Polygon[/b][/url], and other outlets. It's been a source of energy and inspiration for the past several months as we move through updates, bugs, and porting. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/389a9d731755a585bf787654a9308b0fbbbaf7c6.png[/img]

[h2]PATCHES & NEW FEATURES[/h2]
We’ve also received our share of helpful criticism. We've done our best to address what we can. We’ve added the ability to automate combat encounters in the game, provided an “expert mode” for eliminating signposting for more challenging puzzles, made various edits to pieces of the script that were undercooked or too verbose, added full gamepad support & a “chapter select” menu, improved performance, and more. You can always check the latest patch notes [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1221250/discussions/0/3177859358966548754/][b]here[/b][/url]. 

[h2]SOUNDTRACK[/h2]
Not long after launch, the record label Sacred Bones released the [url=https://www.sacredbonesrecords.com/products/sbr310-thou-norco-ost][b]NORCO OST[/b][/url] as a split with our dear friends Thou. We’d been discussing some kind of collaboration with them for a while, and were thrilled for it to finally materialize. The split features extra material, an album's worth of original Thou tracks, and sleeves that double as pixel art prints.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/0fb669910016e0f3ae0437cf260065f43fb58cd1.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/55344861de09cd00f2c6436d4f76b08924bbd41c.png[/img]

[h2]INTERVIEWS, WRITTEN REFLECTIONS & VIDEO ESSAYS[/h2]
Following the release, I spoke to a number of outlets, including [url=https://www.wwno.org/coastal-desk/2022-04-01/q-a-with-the-creator-of-norco-a-transformative-point-and-click-game-exploring-the-south][b]WWNO[/b][/url], [url=https://www.polygon.com/23015306/norco-developer-geography-of-robots-interview-ending][b]Polygon[/b][/url], [url=https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/112-interview-norco-creator-yuts-geography-of-robots/id1498853997?i=1000566074916][b]Gaming in the Wild,[/b][/url] and [url=https://www.audible.com/pd/Episode-475-Interview-with-NORCO-Developer-Yuts-Podcast/B09Y9HQT5X][b]Waypoint[/b][/url]. By the summer, I’d gotten a little tired of hearing myself talk and decided to step back from interviews, but those early conversations were extremely valuable in setting the right context for players to understand the game – its origins, intentions, and how it relates to other regional media. I’m forever grateful for those opportunities. 

There were a number of written essays that resonated deeply, such as “[url=https://eaglestower.wordpress.com/2022/04/21/norco-and-the-art-of-never-going-home/][b]NORCO and the Art of Never Going Home[/b][/url]” by [url=https://twitter.com/lavalampbamboo]Eddie Johnston[/url], as well as “[url=https://lotusrootrecords.neocities.org/writing/posts/2022-09-15-notes-on-norco.html][b]notes on norco[/b][/url]” by [url=https://twitter.com/_earth_seed]lotus[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/b38cd72e6c47e00bd7f92e434fde6be5c77fc295.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/9159324e9bf15b685ddd40d8e092ab931955b88e.png[/img]

Youtube creators shared several thoughtful and in-depth video essays about NORCO, such as this one by [b]RagnaRox[/b] that brilliantly communicates the spirit of the game:

[previewyoutube=pNX280h12Mg;full][/previewyoutube]

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZoDhW8g5xks][b]That Dang Dad[/b][/url] also reflects on the game’s relationship to oil and climate, and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bwPh4uAYMH8][b]The Svamp King[/b][/url] uses hauntological elements of the game as a springboard for discussing lost and alternative futures.

[h2]CONSOLE PORTING[/h2]
This ended up being more of a job than we anticipated, but as of early December, we’re very happy to be on the other side of it. A lot of the technical debt that we accumulated in the lead-up to release came back to haunt us. 

One lesson I learned throughout all of this: avoid crunch at all costs. Not only does it ruin your mental health and your morale, but it leads to messy code that you’ll have to fix in the end. After a couple of big refactors, the code is in a much better place. The 1.4.4 patch should be running more smoothly than 1.4.3 on lower-performance machines. This difference is particularly noticeable on PS4 but should benefit Steam Deck players as well.

We also implemented full controller support for a more console-native experience. You can use the d-pad to navigate discretely, and there are various shortcuts to make navigation and selection easier. This video goes over a few of them: 

[previewyoutube=WL74mv-0onM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]END-OF-THE-YEAR RECOGNITION & PRINTS[/h2]
We’ve received a lot of love the past couple months, and I know I’m repeating myself, but we truly are deeply grateful. NORCO’s not perfect, and we have a lot to learn as first-time devs. But the fact that so many of you believe in and support this experiment means everything. We owe it to those who have helped and supported us to express both our pride and our gratitude.

We were excited to learn that we were nominated for the category of Best Debut Indie at [b]The Game Awards [/b]alongside Stray, Neon White, Tunic, and Vampire Survivors.

We also ended up on several end-of-the-year lists:

[list]
[url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/games/best-games-of-2022/]Paste Magazine’s 30 Best Games of 2022[/url] (WE WERE NUMBER 1….???!!! 😱)
[url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/2022-in-review/the-best-video-games-of-2022]New Yorker Best Video Games of 2022[/url]
[url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/features/the-25-best-video-games-of-2022/]Slant Magazine’s 25 Best Video Games of 2022[/url]
[url=https://www.polygon.com/what-to-play/22956981/best-games-2022-list]Polygon’s 50 Best Games of 2022[/url][/list]

Another welcome development to bookend the year was [b]Lost in Cult[/b]’s limited run of NORCO prints of Jesse Jacobi’s handpainted key art. Many people have requested these, but it’s been hard to find the time to order and ship them, so it’s massively appreciated. You can order them [url=https://www.lostincult.co.uk/shop/p/gotta-go-fast-art-print-pnteb-a93bk][b]here[/b][/url] through February.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/02ae686fe1aba94628792f0f6aeb75aa7b29321e.png[/img]

[h2]THANK YOU![/h2]
While we still have a few patches and features in store for NORCO, we’ll begin focusing on new things. Future projects are certain to carry many of NORCO’s themes forward. We’ll have more to share on that soon.

One last time: thank you, thank you, thank you for sticking with us. We are extremely lucky to have the kind of thoughtful, considerate, and supportive community that we do. It’s an honor.

More soon!
- Yuts

notes.title: NORCO PC Feature Update (Mac soon!); 50% Off Sale
notes.content:
[h3]Hello! 

Version 1.3.2 of NORCO is now live for PC.[/h3] Due to vacation scheduling, we've unfortunately had to delay its Mac release, but it should be available by the end of the month for Mac users as well.

This update includes two new features that players have requested: "Expert Mode" and "Autocombat." Both of these can be found in the "Gameplay" submenu that's now available from the settings menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/c8157fd6569a2a18873039b658f91f7cfe6f8c16.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/889c2297762ebf6d49586af4ad242f2fec457a89.jpg[/img]

[u][b]NEW FEATURE - EXPERT MODE[/b][/u]
This is an idea that user Safe-Keeper suggested [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1221250/discussions/0/3279194062594503369/]in the discussion forum[/url]. This mode eliminates the "hint" highlighting feature from the game, several instances of dialogue hinting and signposting, and certain visual cues that assist in puzzle solving. This is meant to create a more challenging playthrough for experienced adventure game players.

[u][b]NEW FEATURE - AUTOCOMBAT[/b][/u]
This feature automates all combat encounters in the game, with the exception of the Crouton encounter. We decided to leave this one in because it's optional and [spoiler]there's an alternative solution later in the game[/spoiler]. We'd love your feedback if you feel differently about this decision.
[u][b]
50% OFF SALE + STREAM[/b][/u]
NORCO will be 50% off starting August 7th to the 13th. We'll be sitting down with our friend Leigh ([url=https://twitter.com/roaringblood]@roaringblood[/url]) for a casual playthrough and discussion of NORCO's themes. Leigh grew up across the river from Norco and has recently done an "annotated stream" of the game that provides a lot of local insight into the region. This playthrough will be pre-recorded and will be looping [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1221250/NORCO/]here [/url]on the Steam page during the sale.

[u][b]FUTURE UPDATES[/b][/u]
We'll continue to work on quality of life features over the course of the Summer/Fall based on feedback we've received here and in the forum. Something that a couple of players have requested is the ability to scroll back in dialogue. Because of the way we implemented the dialogue system, this will unfortunately require a larger refactor than it would otherwise, but it's something we really hope to implement. We'll keep you posted on this and any other features/content/ideas we're cooking up over the next several months.

Thank you as always for your continued interest and support! It really means a lot,

NORCO devs

notes.title: NORCO诺科 Adds Simplified Chinese Language & Gamepad Support
notes.content:
Hi Everyone, 我们现在有简体中文啦！

[h3]Wanted to let you know there's an update going out today for Simplified Chinese language support.[/h3] If you're interested, there's now a version of the trailer in Simplified Chinese that you can watch on YouTube... or on bilibili!

[previewyoutube=GFUVxU0rUUQ;full][/previewyoutube]

We've also implemented gamepad support. We targeted Xbox controllers this round, though it should work for other gamepads as well. Here's the layout:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/808f43d4273abb09ce285cdf6d14c65e57e9bd9d.png[/img]

You can control the mouse cursor manually using the left joystick or select elements on the screen discretely using the d-pad. You can also jump to elements of different types quickly by using the "cycle" buttons. Whenever you encounter a scrollable screen (computer in the bedroom; phone text messages; using the Apocryphon app; etc), you can use the right analog to scroll. We QA'd this as much as we could but if you hit anything, we'd love if you could submit a ticket [url=http://norcogame.com/releasenotes.html]here[/url].

Thank you as always! We'll have more updates and features coming very soon, including an "expert mode" that eliminates hints from the game to make puzzles more challenging for experienced adventure game players. If you love the game and want to see more from us, please leave a Steam review. It makes a big difference and is a great way to support small indies. Thank you again -

NORCO devs

notes.title: SPANISH, FRENCH, GERMAN, RUSSIAN & BRAZILIAN-PORTUGUESE ADDED TO NORCO TODAY
notes.content:
[h3]Just a quick language update for you today -[/h3] 
If you are reading this then Spanish, French, German, Russian & Brazilian-Portuguese languages are now available in NORCO! Steam will automatically update your version of the game to include these languages. You'll know you are playing the latest version if you see v1.1.0i in the top right corner of the title screen. From there select SETTINGS, then LANGUAGE, then choose your language of choice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/b432b0751113855d868c1fbc1fdf3a9235c1f220.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/221c6544d4ad927185b9aba1d35be1b2b0d52fc7.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/1e6ced04880b94217a32ea8883d26060ae713807.jpg[/img]

NORCO is a narrative game at its heart so it was very important to us that the alternate language versions be as accurate and representative to the source material as possible - so thank you for your continued patience while we polished and got them ready. 

One note: not all languages support all font options in the game. We're working to include additional fonts in future patches.

Thank you again. More updates coming soon,
Y.

notes.title: A.MAZE FEST NOMINATION; FIVE LANGUAGES TO BE ADDED VERY SOON
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/4abb2a0b4bd2a96254b87b145d9cea54f14c0b8d.jpg[/img]

[h3]An endless thank you to everyone who's been continuing to keep up with this project, write reviews, report bugs, and express general positivity and good will.[/h3] It's been a wild few weeks and having friends by our side has made all the difference. Lots has been happening! More very thoughtful and encouraging press reviews have been coming in like this one from [url=https://www.thegamer.com/norco-review-a-narrative-masterpiece/]TheGamer [/url]; we got nominated for a few award categories at the [url=https://2022.amaze-berlin.de/]A.MAZE festival[/url] in Berlin which takes place in May; and Jesse Jacobi and I sat with the wonderful hosts of [url=https://www.redcircle.com/shows/8dc75889-bdb1-42f9-8170-b25a63a601f7]No Cartidge[/url] for a relaxed interview about our pixel process, disaster tourism, influences and lots else.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/86657e9271ce7e1fb2dba19fe0406ff16b9c86fb.png[/img]

We're still plugging away at the game, fixing bugs, preparing patches, and most importantly: working towards localization support. Spanish, French, German, Russian, and Brazilian-Portuguese are coming soon! It's been a more difficult process than we'd hoped, and we're identifying lots of sneaky bugs as we test, but we're in the home stretch. We're hoping to get all of these languages released later this week or early next. THANK YOU (a lot) for your continued patience while we translate, implement, and test.

We are looking into adding additional languages like simplified Chinese and others in a few months – keep an eye out for more updates. As always you can access the latest patch notes and bug submission form [url=http://norcogame.com/releasenotes.html]here[/url].

Much love, more soon, thank you forever, 
NORCO devs

notes.title: NORCO REVIEWS & PATCH NOTES

[b]Controls[/b]

[/list]

Have a great weekend!

notes.title: WATCH THE NORCO LAUNCH TRAILER NOW; PLAY THE FULL GAME IN TWO DAYS
notes.content:
[h2]NORCO will be out in only two more days. [/h2]

Our publisher, Raw Fury, edited together a very lovely launch trailer that was just shown at the MIX's 10th Anniversary Showcase. You can watch the trailer here:

[previewyoutube=PFVhJNfnxCY;full][/previewyoutube]

Raw Fury has also invited us to attend a launch-day livestream of the game. I'll be there along with fellow Geography of Robots dev Aaron Gray and artist Jesse Jacobi to share whatever falls out of our heads. If you want to drop by and ask questions we'll start at 10am PST | 1pm ET | 6pm CET on Thursday, live from the NORCO Steam page.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/3b6f13aaab28b7f0113e27847f020202637f54a5.png[/img]

And just a reminder that you'll be able to get the soundtrack to the game and a digital artbook if you buy the game's "Special Edition" bundle. The artbook has lots of ephemera, sketches, notes, insights into the region of Louisiana where the game takes place, interviews, high resolution exports of in-game environments, etc. And the soundtrack is a split release with our very good friends and collaborators Thou. I'm in love with the music that Gewgawly I composed for NORCO and have attended more Thou shows than I can count so I'm thrilled by the release. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/d37e09ce863378b933d63352cc3ef8466c901d28.png[/img]

But yeah, only two more days 😱. I'm truly grateful and appreciative for your support. Thank you!

Y.

notes.title: NORCO RELEASE ONE WEEK AWAY; TRANSLATION INFO
notes.content:
[h2]One week to go before NORCO launches on PC and Mac...[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/c1cda104bfba6c0d167fc635abc9179486d9659a.gif[/img]

We've been adding to, optimizing, and polishing NORCO right up to the last second. Never pixeled this much in my life. We submitted the "gold build" to Steam and passed cert without issue. The English version is ready to go, but we need a bit of extra time to translate and implement French, German, Spanish, Russian, and Brazilian-Portuguese into the game. NORCO's a narrative game at its heart, so this step feels critical to get right. The game will launch in English only on March 24, but we'll deliver these additional languages very soon.

ALSO the game will be 15% off from March 24-31. If you start playing in English, your save game will carry over when we patch in the other languages shortly after.

I'll update you here on patch timings. Thank you for your patience and understanding and all the support you've shown.

Seven days! 😱

Y.

notes.title: Only Two Weeks Until NORCO Release; Roundup of News & Info
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/9df513c678b6e8ab75ebb5b364581b97b3610125.png[/img]
[h2]With two weeks to go before release...[/h2] 
We've been heads down, killing bugs, polishing dialogue, and sneaking new art into the game past our stalwart producer. Anxiety is high! But it's all coming together. Here's a bunch of ways to engage ahead of release:

[b]Wishlist NORCO –[/b] 
If you haven't wishlisted, please consider doing so – it helps.

[b]Follow the project on twitter –[/b] 
I share a bunch of process shots, photos, etc from the production of the game and also aggregate stuff from other GoR members at [url=https://twitter.com/roboticgeo]@roboticgeo[/url]. If you're interested in this project because of its relationship to the Gulf Coast, psychogeography, pixel art, sound design, mysticism, etc then you might find it interesting.

[b]Play the Act One Demo – [/b]
You can play the entire Act One of the full game right now. The Act One demo lives [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1221250/NORCO/]here [/url]indefinitely, and your saved game will carry over if you decide to purchase the full release.

[b]Explore NORCO Art – [/b]
Our publisher set up [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1682520/Art_of_Fury_Virtual_Gallery/]a virtual art gallery[/url] where you can explore art from the game and get an early look at the content in [i]The Art of NORCO[/i], a digital artbook we're releasing full of pixel art, concept photographs, history and research on Norco, Louisiana, along with lots of ephemera behind the creation of the game. You can bid on NORCO art in [url=https://www.artoffuryauction.com/]an online auction[/url] with proceeds split between [url=https://twitter.com/jacobi_jesse]J Jacobi[/url] (key art painter/fellow pixel artist) and an environmental organization in the New Orleans region.

[b]Listen to music from the game – [/b]
We recently announced the [i]NORCO Original Soundtrack[/i], a collaborative album available March 24 that contains the complete in-game score by Gewgawly I (the Geography of Robots composer) as well as an album's worth of new songs by sludge band Thou, our longtime friends and fellow South Louisiana artists. You can listen to six track samples [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SPX-OkkTJlw&list=PLuwwLD7PTg2h7YZlhpLVTJnCmLLBo_kzl&index=1]here[/url].


Six years down, two weeks to go. Thank you again for following along. It means everything.

Yyyyyyyyy

notes.title: NORCO Teams Up With Fellow South Louisiana Artists, Thou, On Joint Album
notes.content:
[h3]Thou represents an aspect of Louisiana that's close to my heart.[/h3] 
The members know the suburbs of New Orleans and Baton Rouge well. I've personally known Bryan, Thou's singer, for most of my life, and he's been committed to the New Orleans underground music scene for as long as I've known him. He helped keep DIY punk alive in the city throughout the early 2000s during the post-Hurricane Katrina era. 

Thou captures a strange irreverence in their sound and visuals that's specific to the region and is rooted in decades of house shows, zine libraries, urban exploration, protests, and carnival theater. Their style has greatly influenced the design of NORCO, and for that reason it felt natural for Geography of Robots to collaborate with Thou on our soundtrack.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/77308a11c62226f3f448f538856cbf881c802ef8.jpg[/img]

Today we have two announcements – the first is the [b]NORCO Original Soundtrack[/b], a collaborative album available March 24 that contains the complete in-game score by Gewgawly I (Geography of Robots composer) as well as an album's worth of new songs by Thou. We've put out six track samples from the album. Check out the whole playlist [url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLuwwLD7PTg2h7YZlhpLVTJnCmLLBo_kzl]here [/url]or hear some of Thou's 'View of a Burning City':

[previewyoutube=cJexVHXzQ8Y;full][/previewyoutube]

The second announcement is the [b]NORCO Special Edition[/b] bundle, also available March 24. With the bundle you'll get a deal on the base game plus the [b]NORCO Original Soundtrack[/b] and [b]The Art of NORCO[/b] digital artbook all together.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/d37e09ce863378b933d63352cc3ef8466c901d28.png[/img]

We're 3 weeks away from launch! Thank you, sincerely, for all the interest and support that's carried us this far.

Y.

notes.title: NORCO Supports macOS; Play Act One Demo on Mac Today!
notes.content:
[h3]Dear Mac users,[/h3]

I'm pleasantly surprised to share that NORCO will now support macOS in addition to PC when it launches on March 24th. The demo, Act One, is also playable on Mac as of today. None of us have a functional Mac, but recently discovered that the game was nearly compatible with macOS as is, with a few minor tweaks. Sorry to those we kept waiting this long!

In case you missed it four weeks ago, here's our Act One Demo trailer, featuring a music track from metal band, Thou, remixed by NORCO's composer, Gewgawly I.

[previewyoutube=Fjz-z6uO1NM;full][/previewyoutube]

If you want to get a sense of NORCO's vibe first you can check out [url=https://twitter.com/gameralphabeta/status/1491488764954296329?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E1491488764954296329%7Ctwgr%5E%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fpublish.twitter.com%2F%3Fquery%3Dhttps3A2F2Ftwitter.com2Fgameralphabeta2Fstatus2F1491488764954296329widget%3DTweet]@AlphaBetaGamer's[/url] no-commentary playthrough of the demo, or this commentary-filled playthrough by [url=https://twitter.com/RawFury?s=20&t=qnetShTzttQu_Za1a_8C7g]@RawFury's[/url] own Gemma.

Luv ya!

[previewyoutube=Fjz-z6uO1NM;full][/previewyoutube]

Thou represents an aspect of Louisiana that's close to my heart. They capture a kind of strange irreverence in their sound and visuals that's specific to the region and has influenced the game NORCO. It's rooted in decades of house shows, zine libraries, urban exploration, protests, and carnival theater. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/5f5a4961c22e8b620184b3131b5474f8108be1d5.png[/img]

notes.title: EXPANDED NORCO DEMO ACT ONE AVAILABLE ON STEAM JANUARY 20
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36589439/a64acb4309a14f8748e0e24de0e3dd5fc058185e.png[/img]

[h3]We are happy to share that [b]the expanded demo, NORCO Act One, will be available on January 20th[/b] as part of [b]Hitcents’ Big Adventure Event[/b] on Steam. [/h3]

The BAE will showcase a huge array of breathtaking adventure games from January 20-24, and we are proud and humbled for NORCO to take part with a much updated and polished demo experience. If you played the original NORCO demo last summer then you’ll immediately notice the redrawn art and redesigned UI, plus tons of new dialogue and a new interactive segment added. This time around the demo will stay up indefinitely, and your saved game will carry over if you decide to purchase the full release. 

I’m proud of what we’ve been able to accomplish these last months. I couldn't ask for better friends and collaborators than the ones who've assembled around the project, both on the dev and the publisher side. Thank you to everyone involved and to those who have helped us feel supported as we work towards release.

I'm sharing a few of the newly drawn environments you'll get to explore next week. Enjoy Act One and make sure to check out some other great demos from #theBAE on the 20th.

Sending Love, Y.
